articles.title: El Nino Is Here. India's Monsoon Season Faces Its Biggest Threat in a Decade.
articles.excerpt: U.S. and Indian forecasters have confirmed El Nino conditions that could slash rainfall, shrink harvests, and push food prices higher as 200 million rain-fed farming households begin sowing.
articles.image_caption: A farmer working in a rice paddy field during monsoon rains in Chandrakona, India
articles.nri_angle: NRI families in agricultural states face higher food prices and increased remittance demand as a weak monsoon threatens rural incomes and consumption.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kevin Warsh Chairs His First Fed Meeting This Week. Here Is Why NRIs Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: The new Federal Reserve chairman presides over a pivotal policy decision on Wednesday as inflation climbs, rate hike odds rise, and every signal from Washington ripples through India's rupee, bond markets, and NRI investment portfolios.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the White House, May 22, 2026
articles.nri_angle: NRIs face direct consequences from the Fed's rate path — from U.S. mortgage rates and investment returns to rupee exchange rates and the attractiveness of India-bound deposit schemes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The G7 Has Opened in Evian. Iran, Trade, and India's Seat at the Table Are All in Play.
articles.excerpt: Modi arrives at the French lakeside summit with a dense agenda: the Iran peace deal, a Trump bilateral on Wednesday, and the visa question that won't go away.
articles.image_caption: World leaders at a G7 summit group photo
articles.nri_angle: The G7 agenda — Iran oil prices, US-India trade talks, and H-1B visa policy — directly shapes the economic and immigration landscape for millions of NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Markets Surge as Iran Peace Deal Sends Oil Below $84 and Revives Inflow Hopes.
articles.excerpt: Nifty jumps 1.5 per cent, rupee heads for 94.80, and BlackRock says India's $30 billion selloff was overdone. Here is what NRIs should know.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: RBI's new FCNR deposit window and a strengthening rupee make NRI remittances and property investments cheaper — if the oil price drop holds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gujarat Has Launched Its Industrial Policy 2026. It Wants Semiconductor Factories, Ultra Mega Projects, and NRI Capital.
articles.excerpt: The state expands its priority sectors from nine to sixteen, creates a new category for ₹10,000 crore investments, and puts green manufacturing at the centre of its pitch.
articles.image_caption: Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel at an official event
articles.nri_angle: Gujarat's semiconductor push, green manufacturing incentives, and GIFT City expansion create new investment channels for the state's 10-million-strong global diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Deploy Air Force Planes to Guard Its Medical Exam. Here Is How the NEET Scandal Unravelled.
articles.excerpt: The CBI has arrested 13 people, a headmistress confessed to leaking the physics paper, and 22 lakh students must now retake the test under military-grade security on June 21.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster III transport aircraft — the IAF is being tasked with ferrying NEET exam papers to prevent leaks (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI families with children or relatives preparing for medical entrance exams face uncertainty about the integrity of India's examination system.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Factories Are Losing 40 Per Cent of Their Output to Heat. The Economic Cost Could Hit 4.5 Per Cent of GDP.
articles.excerpt: In Kanpur, workers are collapsing or returning to their villages. New research shows the growth hit from rising temperatures is nearly double what economists previously believed.
articles.image_caption: Workers in an Indian factory — extreme heat is cutting factory output by up to 40 per cent across the country (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with investments in Indian manufacturing and families back home face growing risks from a heat crisis that is cutting factory output and threatening the health of vulnerable relatives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Has Cut Off India From Anthropic's Best AI. Bengaluru Is Building Its Own.
articles.excerpt: The US blocked Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals. India's Sarvam AI has raised $300 million and trained a 105-billion-parameter model for Indian languages. The sovereign AI race is on.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, whose most advanced AI models are now restricted from export to India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian technologists in the US face export controls based on nationality, while NRI investors see a new asset class emerging in India's sovereign AI ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Is Taking the Exam Scandal Fight to Kota. Here Is What Congress Is Demanding.
articles.excerpt: A nationwide campaign against paper leaks and CBSE failures starts on June 17, with student conventions planned across four cities. The party wants NEET decentralised and the education minister gone.
articles.image_caption: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, who will lead student conventions starting June 17 in Kota
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of NRI and OCI students sit for CBSE board exams and NEET every year — a compromised examination system directly threatens the merit-based pathway that diaspora families count on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US-Iran Deal Is Done. Oil Has Dropped 4 Per Cent. Here Is What It Means for India.
articles.excerpt: The Strait of Hormuz will reopen immediately. The naval blockade is over. A signing ceremony is set for Friday in Switzerland. And India's oil import bill just got significantly lighter.
articles.image_caption: Map of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that carries a fifth of the world's oil
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper crude oil means a stronger rupee, lower petrol prices in India, and relief for NRIs watching the currency slide all year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Meets Trump Wednesday at G7. Trade, Visas, and Three Dead Sailors Are All on the Table.
articles.excerpt: The bilateral comes as Washington threatens a 12.5 per cent tariff, H-1B approvals have dropped 40 per cent, and India has twice summoned the U.S. envoy over the killing of Indian sailors in the Gulf.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France
articles.nri_angle: The meeting will determine whether the 12.5% tariff threat is walked back, whether H-1B processing gets relief, and whether Trump acknowledges the sailor deaths — all issues that directly affect NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Will Build a 168-Megawatt AI Data Centre Inside Ambani's Jamnagar Complex. Here Is Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: The deal deepens Meta's partnership with Reliance, positions India as an AI infrastructure hub, and arrives just as Anthropic's access restrictions have reignited the sovereign AI debate.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, whose Jamnagar complex will host Meta's new AI data centre
articles.nri_angle: India's AI infrastructure is moving from government promises to concrete projects — creating high-skilled jobs, boosting Jio Platforms' IPO profile, and potentially reducing dependence on foreign AI providers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's Top Trade Negotiator Is Coming to India. A Deal Could Land by Mid-July.
articles.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer will visit New Delhi after the G7 Summit to advance a bilateral trade agreement — but dead Indian sailors in the Gulf have added a volatile new dimension to the talks.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who will visit India after the G7 Summit for trade negotiations
articles.nri_angle: A U.S.-India trade deal directly affects NRIs through tariff structures on remitted goods, pharmaceutical pricing, IT services market access, and the broader economic relationship that shapes visa and immigration policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Have Drawn Up a Five-Year Plan to Double Trade. Here Is Everything They Agreed at Villa Kerylos.
articles.excerpt: An Innovation Roadmap 2030, a joint AI working group, a new dialogue on critical minerals, and 19 signed agreements — the Nice summit delivered substance, not just ceremony.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron during a bilateral meeting
articles.nri_angle: The bilateral outcomes directly affect NRIs through visa-free French airport transit, expanded education pathways, and a trade mechanism that could reshape India's commercial access to all 27 EU member states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tech Leaders Are Demanding a $6 Billion AI Fund. The Anthropic Shutdown Made It Personal.
articles.excerpt: Mohandas Pai wants ₹50,000 crore a year for sovereign AI. Sridhar Vembu says go open-source. Both agree on one thing: India cannot build its future on infrastructure it does not control.
articles.image_caption: India's top tech leaders are demanding a sovereign AI fund after Anthropic's service restrictions in India exposed the country's dependence on foreign AI providers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers on H-1B visas at U.S. AI companies are now classified alongside all foreign nationals under the new export controls — making this both a policy story and a personal one for the diaspora workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Now Under Fire From Both Sides in the Gulf. The U.S. Struck Its Sailors. Trump Says Iran Attacked Its Ships Too.
articles.excerpt: Three Indian seafarers are dead from a U.S. Navy strike. Hours later, Trump accused Iran of launching drones at Indian vessels. Jaishankar called Rubio to protest. India's 300,000 merchant sailors are caught in the middle of a war they played no part in starting.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who called U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to lodge a strong protest over the killing of Indian sailors
articles.nri_angle: India is the world's second-largest supplier of merchant seafarers — over 300,000 globally. Many NRI families in coastal states have relatives working on vessels in the Gulf, and the escalating attacks have triggered panic across the maritime community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Judge Killed the $100,000 H-1B Fee. Four Days Later, He Froze His Own Ruling.
articles.excerpt: The legal seesaw has left Indian tech workers in limbo as Trump appeals and Congress moves to codify the fee permanently.
articles.image_caption: Judge Leo Sorokin, who ruled the $100,000 H-1B fee unconstitutional
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for over 70% of all H-1B petitions — the fee's fate directly determines whether hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals can afford to work in the United States.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Waived Customs Duty on Nuclear Equipment Going Back Seven Years. The Market Noticed.
articles.excerpt: The retrospective exemption formalises an unwritten practice, cuts project costs, and sends nuclear stocks surging as India chases 100 GW by 2047.
articles.image_caption: A nuclear power plant in India — the government has waived customs duty on equipment imports going back seven years
articles.nri_angle: The nuclear duty waiver and 100 GW target create a multi-decade infrastructure investment opportunity for NRIs tracking India's energy transition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Wants Diaspora Athletes to Play for the National Team. The 'Sports Passport' Is Now on Modi's Desk.
articles.excerpt: The Sports Ministry has sent a proposal to the PM's Office and the Home Ministry that would let PIO and OCI athletes represent India without full citizenship — a move that could reshape the country's Olympic and FIFA ambitions.
articles.image_caption: Indian football fans — the Blue Pilgrims — rallying in support of the national team at a 2018 match in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora athletes of Indian origin — many trained in elite sporting systems in Europe, North America, and Australia — could finally represent India under this framework, connecting the global Indian community to the country's sporting future.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Lands in Slovakia. No Indian Prime Minister Has Set Foot There Since 1993.
articles.excerpt: Bilateral trade has doubled to €1.6 billion in three years. The first-ever visit comes as the India-EU Free Trade Agreement opens new doors for Slovak and Indian businesses alike.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an official portrait
articles.nri_angle: The visit strengthens India-EU economic ties, with the recently concluded FTA expected to double trade and create new investment and employment pathways for NRIs and Indian businesses in Central Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Top IT Firms Got 40 Per Cent Fewer H-1B Visas This Year. TCS Was Hit the Hardest.
articles.excerpt: The $100,000 visa fee and a wage-weighted lottery are pushing the industry towards offshore work and local US hiring. The American dream is getting harder for 1.9 million IT employees.
articles.image_caption: H-1B visa application trends in the United States
articles.nri_angle: The 40% drop in H-1B approvals directly impacts hundreds of thousands of Indian IT professionals hoping to work in the US, while the simultaneous crackdown on green cards and adjustment of status is disrupting long-term career plans for those already there.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Now Wants Green Card Applicants to Leave the Country. Zoho's Founder Says They Should.
articles.excerpt: A new USCIS policy redefines Adjustment of Status as 'extraordinary relief,' pushing H-1B holders into overseas processing. Sridhar Vembu's response: 'Please come home.'
articles.image_caption: A US permanent resident card, commonly known as a green card
articles.nri_angle: The policy directly disrupts the lives of tens of thousands of Indian H-1B and L-1 holders who had planned careers around adjusting status domestically, forcing them to weigh leaving the US against an uncertain consular timeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Iran Deal Draft Is Out. Here Is What Is in It — and What India Stands to Gain.
articles.excerpt: Iran has reportedly agreed to abandon its nuclear weapons programme. The US will release roughly $20 billion in frozen assets and waive oil sanctions. The Strait of Hormuz — which carried 40 per cent of India's crude imports — would reopen immediately.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz and the Musandam Peninsula — the chokepoint Iran has blockaded since February
articles.nri_angle: A reopened Strait of Hormuz would ease India's energy costs, lower inflation, and stabilise the rupee — all of which directly affect NRI remittances, investments, and the cost of travel home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Opened Its Stock Market to Every Foreigner. NRIs Are No Longer the Only Ones Who Can Buy In.
articles.excerpt: A sweeping FEMA amendment notified on June 12 lets any individual living outside India invest in listed Indian companies — ending a decades-old framework that restricted the route to NRIs and OCIs alone.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who previously had exclusive access to Indian portfolio investments through FEMA now share that route with all foreign individuals, potentially reshaping competition and liquidity in Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Have Opened 'Bharat Innovates' in Nice. 120 Indian Startups Are Pitching to European Capital.
articles.excerpt: The three-day conclave at the Palais des Expositions has brought together 500 investors, 15 top Indian universities, and a startup cohort that holds 1,500 patents and has raised over $1.5 billion collectively.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who jointly inaugurated the Bharat Innovates 2026 conclave with French President Emmanuel Macron in Nice
articles.nri_angle: An estimated 119,000 Indians live in mainland France and over 350,000 in French overseas territories — the conclave offers the diaspora direct access to India's expanding deep-tech ecosystem and investment opportunities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRI Dollar Deposits at Rates Not Seen in a Decade. The RBI Is Picking Up the Tab.
articles.excerpt: SBI, HDFC, ICICI, and Kotak have all hiked FCNR(B) rates to as high as 7.1 per cent after the central bank agreed to absorb the full hedging cost. Analysts say $60–70 billion could flow in by September.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn up to 7.1% on dollar deposits in Indian banks — the highest in a decade — with zero currency hedging risk, as the RBI absorbs the cost until September 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Rejected Washington's 'Forced Labour' and 'Surplus Capacity' Charges. The 12.5 Per Cent Tariff Threat Is Now Part of the Deal.
articles.excerpt: As USTR Jamieson Greer prepares to fly to India the week after the G7, New Delhi is pushing for an assurance that no new tariffs will follow the bilateral trade agreement. Both sides say mid-July is possible.
articles.image_caption: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who will visit India after the G7 summit
articles.nri_angle: A US-India trade deal — the first in 75 years — could push bilateral trade toward $500 billion and directly affect millions of Indian Americans and Indian businesses operating across both economies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian Sailors Are Dead After U.S. Navy Strikes. Delhi Has Summoned the American Envoy Twice.
articles.excerpt: The Settebello strike killed three merchant mariners from UP, Himachal and Andhra. India is furious. Washington says comply or face consequences.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Navy ships operating in the Gulf of Oman, where three Indian-crewed tankers were struck this week
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers, overwhelmingly from middle-class families across UP, Kerala, Maharashtra and AP, are the sole earners sending remittances home — any sustained threat to maritime safety directly impacts household economies across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Says the U.S. Asked India to Buy Russian Oil. Then It Imposed Tariffs.
articles.excerpt: At Finland’s Kultaranta Talks, India’s foreign minister laid out the receipts: Washington needed Indian refiners to stabilise crude markets in 2022. Now it is taxing them.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar at an official event
articles.nri_angle: A breakdown in India-U.S. trade talks could ripple through H-1B processing goodwill, tariff exemptions on Indian goods, and the diplomatic climate NRI professionals depend on for business and immigration stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Just Handed 50,000 Employees an AI Co-Worker. India's IT Industry Is Bracing for What Comes Next.
articles.excerpt: The Anthropic deal is the biggest enterprise AI deployment by an Indian company — and the clearest signal yet that the $315 billion IT services model is being rebuilt from the inside.
articles.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services is deploying AI co-workers to 50,000 employees, signalling a structural shift in India's IT industry
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRI tech workers depend on India's IT services industry — the AI transformation underway at TCS directly affects their job security, career trajectory, and the value of their skills.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Has Also Run Out of EB-5 Investor Green Cards for Indians. The Queue Will Not Move Until October.
articles.excerpt: A week after EB-2 visas hit their annual cap, the investor pathway has followed suit — leaving wealthy Indian applicants with no route to permanent residency until the new fiscal year begins.
articles.image_caption: A United States permanent resident card — Indian EB-5 investor applicants will see no new green cards issued until the fiscal year resets in October (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian investors who have committed hundreds of thousands of dollars to U.S. businesses now face months of limbo, with no EB-5 visas available until October — the second employment-based pathway to close on them in a week.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Want a U.S. Visa Interview in Ten Days? That Will Be $750, Please.
articles.excerpt: The State Department will let B1/B2 visa applicants pay their way to the front of the queue starting July 1. For an Indian family of four, the total visa bill could top ₹3 lakh.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Embassy in New Delhi — the State Department's new premium appointment service will let visa applicants pay 50 for a guaranteed interview within ten business days (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian families visiting relatives in America could face visa bills exceeding ₹3 lakh for a family of four under the new premium appointment scheme — adding financial strain to an already slow and uncertain process.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Belfast Is Burning. India's Cricket Tour of Ireland May Be the Next Casualty.
articles.excerpt: Anti-immigration riots in Northern Ireland have put India's two-match T20I series in doubt. The BCCI is monitoring the situation, and a venue change is on the table.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Indians living in Belfast are anxious as anti-immigration riots grip the city — and the scheduled India cricket tour to Stormont could be relocated, depriving the local diaspora of a rare opportunity to watch the national team play.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the U.S. Just Signed a Ten-Year Defence Framework. It Covers Everything From Javelins to Jets.
articles.excerpt: Rajnath Singh and Pete Hegseth formalised the agreement on the sidelines of ADMM-Plus in Kuala Lumpur, calling it the beginning of a 'new chapter' in bilateral defence ties.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at an official engagement in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: A deeper India-U.S. defence relationship affects everything from visa climate to bilateral trade for the 4.4 million Indian-Americans in the United States.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Staffing CEO Forged H-1B Petitions for Years. Now the DOJ Is Revoking His Citizenship.
articles.excerpt: Neeraj Sharma of New Jersey is one of 17 naturalized citizens targeted in the largest denaturalization sweep in American history. USCIS has been asked to supply 100 to 200 cases per month.
articles.image_caption: The Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: With 100-200 denaturalization cases being referred monthly, naturalized Indian-Americans face a new era of scrutiny where past immigration applications are never truly closed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX's $75 Billion IPO Makes Musk the First Trillionaire. Indian Investors Are Scrambling to Get In.
articles.excerpt: Indian investment platforms report 'unprecedented' traffic as retail investors chase the world's largest stock offering through LRS and US-listed intermediaries.
articles.image_caption: SpaceX's Starbase facility in Boca Chica, Texas, headquarters of the newly public company
articles.nri_angle: Indian investors can access SpaceX through LRS-compliant platforms, with FY26 foreign equity remittances already up 56 per cent — this listing accelerates a structural shift in cross-border capital flows from India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Markets Post Best Day in Two Months. Oil Crashed. The Rupee Rallied. Foreign Money May Follow.
articles.excerpt: Sensex surged 1,695 points and the rupee hit 95.11 as Brent crude fell below $87 on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal. Analysts say the record $30 billion in foreign outflows may finally reverse.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who pulled back during the oil shock may find a peace deal, falling crude, and a strengthening rupee create a fundamentally different risk-reward equation for Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Student Posted His Answer Sheet Online. It Wasn't His Handwriting. India's Largest Exam Board Is Now in Crisis.
articles.excerpt: CBSE's on-screen marking system swapped answer sheets, exposed student data through security flaws, and survived coordinated cyber attacks — all within weeks of launch. Parliament has stepped in.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRI families rely on CBSE board results as a foundational credential — the scandal undermines trust in the system that evaluates over 40 lakh students annually.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Inflation Just Hit Its Highest Level of 2026. Food and Fuel Are Doing the Damage.
articles.excerpt: Retail prices rose 3.93 per cent in May — still below the RBI's 4 per cent target, but accelerating fast. The central bank has already revised its full-year forecast to 5.1 per cent.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — the central bank faces mounting pressure as retail inflation hits a 2026 high (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Rising food and fuel inflation will hit remittance-dependent families hardest — the rupees NRIs send home are buying less each month, and a weak monsoon could make it worse.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Says Iran Deal Will Be Signed Sunday. The Strait of Hormuz Will Reopen 'Immediately.'
articles.excerpt: The announcement sent crude prices tumbling to a two-month low and triggered India's best market day in two months. But Tehran says it has not yet finalised a signing date.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Navy ships transit the Strait of Hormuz, the critical oil shipping lane at the centre of the conflict
articles.nri_angle: A reopened Hormuz would ease global crude prices, directly lowering fuel and grocery costs for NRIs, while reducing the risk to Indian seafarers who have been caught in the crossfire.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Will Inaugurate India's Largest Deep-Tech Showcase in Nice Tomorrow. 120 Startups Made the Cut.
articles.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026 brings Indian founders in semiconductors, space, biotech and quantum computing to the French Riviera. Twenty-eight MoUs with French and international partners are expected.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron at an earlier bilateral meeting
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin founders and researchers in Europe and the US now have a direct government-backed platform to connect with French capital and research labs — this is the India-France innovation corridor coming alive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Dead After IAF An-32 Crashes at Jorhat. The Fleet Has Killed Over 100 in Four Decades.
articles.excerpt: The Soviet-era workhorse broke apart on the runway. Its replacement was promised years ago. It still has not arrived.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force Antonov An-32 transport aircraft in flight
articles.nri_angle: Two of the five dead were Agnipath recruits — the crash highlights the human cost of India's aging military fleet and the gap between defence modernisation announcements and ground reality.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: White House Confirms Trump Will Meet Modi on Wednesday at the G7. Trade, Visas and the Iran War Are All on the Table.
articles.excerpt: It will be their first face-to-face meeting in over a year. The USTR will fly to India the following week to close a deal.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an official portrait
articles.nri_angle: The Trump-Modi bilateral will directly affect H-1B visa policy, India-US trade deals, and the Iran war's impact on oil prices and Indian seafarer safety.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Just Ordered Anthropic to Shut Down Its Most Powerful AI Models. Foreign Nationals Need Not Apply.
articles.excerpt: The Commerce Department's export control directive blocks all non-Americans from accessing Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — including H-1B holders working inside the United States.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, whose company was forced to disable its most advanced AI models
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian tech workers in the US on H-1B visas — many of whom build with Anthropic's models daily — are classified as foreign nationals under this order and could be locked out of frontier AI tools.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Has Run Out of EB-2 Green Cards for Indians. The Queue Will Not Move Until October.
articles.excerpt: Every EB-2 visa number allocated to India for the fiscal year has been used. Processing is frozen until the annual reset on October 1, leaving at least 28,000 approved applicants in limbo.
articles.image_caption: kevin dooley via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: The EB-2 freeze directly affects tens of thousands of Indian professionals in the US who have been waiting years — sometimes over a decade — for permanent residency despite having approved petitions and stable jobs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Applicants to US Law Schools Have Dropped 23 Per Cent. The Visa Climate Is Driving Them Away.
articles.excerpt: America denied 35 per cent of international student visa applications last year — the highest rate in a decade. Indian LL.M. applicants are increasingly choosing the UK and Europe instead.
articles.image_caption: Areeda Hall at Harvard Law School, one of several elite US law programmes reporting sharp declines in international applications
articles.nri_angle: Indian families who have historically invested heavily in US legal education for their children are now reconsidering the value proposition as visa uncertainty, rising costs, and anti-immigrant rhetoric make American campuses feel less welcoming.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: El Niño Has Arrived. India's Monsoon Is Already 26 Per Cent Below Normal.
articles.excerpt: Forecasters say this could be the strongest El Niño since 1997. Farmers are switching crops. Food prices may follow.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: A weak monsoon could trigger food inflation that hits NRI families in rural India and tighten global rice markets where India is the largest exporter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar May Visit Canada Next Week. It Would Be the First High-Level Trip Since the Diplomatic Freeze.
articles.excerpt: Mark Carney is pivoting away from Washington and toward New Delhi. India is listening — but wants action on Khalistan first.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar
articles.nri_angle: 1.8 million Indian Canadians have endured visa delays and consular shutdowns during the diplomatic freeze — a thaw could restore services and open new trade corridors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's Top Trade Negotiator Will Fly to India the Week After G7. A Deal, Officials Say, Is Possible.
articles.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer's visit follows months of back-and-forth on tariffs, Section 301 probes, and a bilateral framework that could reshape how NRIs send goods — and money — across both countries.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at his official portrait session
articles.nri_angle: A US-India trade deal directly affects NRI remittances, tariffs on Indian exports, H-1B visa policy, and the cost of goods flowing between the two countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata's iPhone Parts Factory Faces Shutdown Threat After Regulators Find Contaminated Farmland Water.
articles.excerpt: Tamil Nadu's pollution board says wastewater from Tata Electronics' Hosur plant overflowed into nearby agricultural wells. Tata says its own tests show full compliance.
articles.image_caption: Hosur, Tamil Nadu, where Tata Electronics operates its iPhone parts manufacturing plant (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's rise as a global iPhone manufacturing hub is a point of pride for the diaspora — but recurring supply chain problems raise questions about whether growth is outpacing environmental governance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
